title: Claude Code vs GitHub Copilot
summary: Choose between coding workflows by testing the same repository task, account policy and review loop.

sections.heading: Use the same issue and repository
paragraphs: Give each candidate the same bounded maintenance task, acceptance test and clean branch. Record which files changed, how easy it was to inspect the proposed work and how much setup the developer needed to complete it.

sections.heading: Separate workflow fit from account policy
paragraphs: The current profiles describe different entry points and plan-dependent features. Confirm the actual IDE, terminal, organization policy and account type you will use; do not combine a feature from one plan with the price or privacy terms of another.

sections.heading: Compare total review effort
paragraphs: Measure accepted and rejected changes, repair time and command review. Keep tests and permission boundaries identical. A faster first response does not establish a safer or less expensive result.

pros.text: Claude Code documents local stdio and remote HTTP or WebSocket MCP servers.
GitHub documents both manual MCP server configuration and installation through the GitHub MCP Registry for VS Code.

cons.text: Claude Code project-scoped MCP servers require workspace trust and approval; a cloned repository cannot approve its own servers.
The documented Copilot MCP path requires VS Code 1.99 or later, and Business or Enterprise organization members need the MCP policy enabled.

faqs.question: Does GitHub's MCP organization policy govern individual Copilot plans?
faqs.answer: No. GitHub scopes that policy to organization or enterprise members on Business or Enterprise plans, not Free, Pro, Pro+ or Max plans.

faqs.question: Can a cloned repository approve its own Claude Code MCP servers?
faqs.answer: No. Project server settings are not approved until the workspace is trusted; review and approve the server in the trusted workspace.

verdict: Let your real repository task and account requirements decide. Confirm current plan entitlements and privacy settings before making a team-level recommendation.
bestFor: Developers comparing a coding-agent workflow with IDE assistance and GitHub features
notFor: Teams requiring an already-verified account-specific privacy, entitlement or cost conclusion
migration: Trial the replacement on a branch while preserving the current review workflow. Recheck organization policy, account access and repository instructions before moving team usage.
gaps: GitHub Copilot feature availability and privacy settings depend on the account or organization; verify the exact deployment before publication.
This comparison contains no hands-on benchmark or measured task result.
